notes.title: Update Notes for May 11, 2023
notes.notes:
What's new
[olist]
 The database connection status for the non-DLC content changed. The thumbnail Artwork matches the community artwork for the Database Gates DLC. If you don't own the DLC, it will change to a technical readout on mouse over and indicate that it's DLC when clicked.
 Cellular analysis integrated beneath the big yellow main information button.
 Quantum State Processor. added to the meddigagoe digital flipbook animation. When not in use the processor is shown. This detail helps balance out the overall balance of shape and color additions,
 Memory block artwork beneath was redesigned beneath to tie into the new design work.
 The 3 lower 3D reconstruction buttons are now in perfect alignment. The meddigagoe button was offset. A minor bug was fixed.
 Meddigagoe digital flipbook animation dots not have a collision detector that displays an off white background between the frames to reduce flicker. Before the color matched the dark grey background  of the overall composition.
 Preloading artwork added. This is seen before the main title screen. The idea is that we are seeing the formation of the microscope interface that will be ready to use at the end of the loading sequence. This is  generative artwork in that it changes and is totally different every time Integument is launched.
 New Spot Illustration added. This replaces a previous one. Spot illustrations had their vibrance boosted to reflect and balance the overall color changes across Integument and its DLC.
 The new spot illustration come with new blortus anatomical diagrams that include labeled features and an audio lab note.
 There is also more real-time animation of information being transferred between the blortus and the DNA base pair molecules.  I tend to save this kind of thing for the DLC since I want this to still be considered an illustration even through obviously it's something else. However, this particular piece really needed to have the special treatment primarily because the human reference :)
 Main window will now revert normal status after syncing. Before it was still displaying "SYNC 100%" after completion.
 Real-time animated progress strip added beneath the "mematron" signature.  This replaces the base pair generator. I found this to be more interesting.
 Added more detail to across several traces. Some of them connect to the progress strip.
[/olist]
FIXES
Window icon flashing fixed. It was flickering in the taskbar and window border. The reference to it in the code was in the wrong place.

notes.title: Update notes for April 17, 2023
notes.notes:
Hada Microbiome Area Scan 04: ACTIVATED!
New detailed illustrations of hada predator called a, Meddigagoe. These are the same creatures in hot pursuit of the blortuses on the main screen (hood). This new screen has some slick interactivity coming from technology used for the DLC.

[olist]
 Spot illustration buttons have enhanced looks. Design cues from their contents has been carried around them.
 More details near and the 4 Spot illustrations to balance out the additional color shapes near the spot illustrations.
 Spot illustration buttons will now activate after a mouse click instead of a mouse press. This prevents accidental launching of multiple windows with a long mouse press.
[/olist]

Changes
[olist]
 Integument preload screen changed from black to a soft dark blue.
 Loading progress percentage animation in outer window frames.
 Integument new splash screen. This was done to reflect and connect the current design language.
 Meddigagoe run animation in the lower level interface (engine) was changed from a movie of an animation loop to a real-time animation loop. Calculating frames can sometimes be less resource intensive than playing a movie.
 The Data Stack Screen (DSS), Animation color grid no longer is always on by will only turn on when you mouse over it.
 Mematron signature When clicked the music playing will have a visual indicator that will stop its animation once the music has stopped.
 Meddigaggoe and blortus technical readouts are all now tidied up. These are the small colorful blinking texts on the sides of some of the windows. They where not lined up perfectly. This all hand coded so yes, it was a pain to do but it was really getting on my nerves!
 Personal Log 01: interface now displays a very cool / atypical waveform when the log entry is being played. Once the personal log has stopped playing the play indicator and waveform will automatically turn off. The lights used to stay on even after the recording had ended.
 TBN (Translation Buffer Node) The rotating thingamabob located in the middle of the "Hood" (Lower level screen interface). One of the orbital nodes was brought back into orbit. It had been rotating around the center of the Data sphere off screen. In cleaning up my code this was revealed.
 
[/olist]

And then...
I refactored all 5961 lines of code that make up, "Integument." This is the programmer equivalent of Spring Cleaning. It's a lot of work but it makes it easier to introduce new content. This isn't a new thing as I rewrite portions of it between updates. It allows me to solve problems, answer questions and discover new things that in turn cause problems, present new questions and challenges.

notes.title: Update notes for February 16, 2023
notes.notes:
The addition of a button to access, Hada Microbiome Area Scan 02. This reveals a snapshot of a preliminary scan of a human face. It's purpose is to locate, identify and catalog unique Hada lifeforms. You may access this new information by clicking on the second colorized spot illustration (male icon) at the bottom of the interface (Engine) and to the left of the "Personal Log 01" buttons.

Over time this information will unpack to reveal more details.

Additionally activity indicator lights (blinkies) have been added to both, Hada Microbiome Area Scan 01 and 02. This is reflected inside both modules once launched.

Several new illustrations, animations and custom code has been prepared to let you experience a closer look of a hada classified as a, Deuro Flea. The cows of the skin, otherwise known as, Integument.

notes.title: Visual and not so visual update
notes.notes:
Lots of minor changes across the board.  These affect the GUI and the underlying code for "Integument" and "Integument - Database: Gates DLC." 

Changes made to, Integument:
[olist]
Many small texts made a bit more readable.
Rotating data wheel in the middle of the "Engine" is now interactive with new art.  New animations and design inspired by a time piece.  It represents the intersection between the pure data and the start of the sorting process.  This was fun to make, so pretty in an industrial designer type way.
B/W Meddigagoe keyframe run animation is consistent. This is the only animation that's not being made in real-time. It's somewhat interactive too.
Text display of DNA base pairs (Base pair generator).
User login name "mematron" moved to the top of the screen.
New music added.  You'll have to search for it.
Added code to cleanly shutdown Java processes specifically used for when Integument is run. Not quite a memory leak but it had the same effect. As Han Solo says, "It's not my fault!"
Minor animation added to Spot Illustration 01.
Most of the green and blue memory cells are now active. What's a "memory cell?!"  You'll figure it out. I trust you ːsteamthumbsupː
"Database Offline," animation color changed to better match the overall color language.
Added several small illustrations to introduce more color variations. This also represents the idea that the computer system is processing new types information and changing it's appearance to reflect that.
[/olist]

Changes made to, Integument - Database: Gates

Added code to cleanly shutdown Java processes specifically used for when Integument is run. Not quite a memory leak but it had the same effect. As Han Solo says, "It's not my fault!"

notes.title: Update notes for January 15, 2023
notes.notes: Added 4 new spot illustrations in "Integument."  They are located near the bottom of lower level (engine) to the left of the "Personal Log" buttons.  They will allow for a fun way of adding new imagery to the application and in a way a preview of things to come. They start off grey and will fill with color once available.
